facts.process_name: Request public records from a Virginia public body
facts.trigger: A requester asks a Virginia public body for public records

trigger_source.quote: all public records shall be open to citizens of the Commonwealth

actors.name: Requester (Virginia citizen or in-state media representative)

source.quote: citizens of the Commonwealth, representatives of newspapers and magazines with circulation in the Commonwealth, and representatives of radio and television stations broadcasting in or into the Commonwealth

actors.name: Public body that is custodian of the records

source.quote: Any public body that is subject to this chapter and that is the custodian of the requested records
Any public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond to a request for records
A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.

steps.action: Require payment of overdue prior-request charges

source.quote: Before processing a request for records, a public body may require the requester to pay any amounts owed to the public body for previous requests for records that remain unpaid 30 days or more after billing.

steps.action: Notify requester of charges; offer cost estimate

source.quote: Prior to conducting a search for records, the public body shall notify the requester in writing that the public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for requested records

steps.action: Ask for an advance cost estimate

source.quote: inquire of the requester whether he would like to request a cost estimate in advance of the supplying of the requested records
The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.
If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn.
The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the cost estimate and the response of the requester.

steps.action: Require deposit up to advance charge determination

source.quote: In any case where a public body determines in advance that charges for producing the requested records are likely to exceed $200, the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
The deposit shall be credited toward the final cost of supplying the requested records.

steps.action: Provide records or give written response

source.quote: promptly, but in all cases within five working days of receiving a request
provide the requested records to the requester or make one of the following responses in writing

steps.action: State conditions making timely response impossible

source.quote: It is not practically possible to provide the requested records or to determine whether they are available within the five-work-day period. Such response shall specify the conditions that make a response impossible.

steps.action: Give one of the four responses

deadline.anchor: end of the five-work-day period (an 'additional' seven work days)

source.quote: If the response is made within five working days, the public body shall have an additional seven work days
in which to provide one of the four preceding responses

steps.action: Try to agree production terms with requester

source.quote: Before proceeding with the petition, however, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to reach an agreement with the requester concerning the production of the records requested.

steps.action: Petition court for more time to respond

source.quote: Any public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond to a request for records

steps.action: Rule on petition for additional time

source.quote: when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search, and a response by the public body within the time required by this chapter will prevent the public body from meeting its operational responsibilities

steps.action: Give access by inspection or copies

source.quote: Access to such records shall be provided by the custodian in accordance with this chapter by inspection or by providing copies of the requested records, at the option of the requester.

steps.action: Release part; describe and cite withheld portions

source.quote: The requested records are being provided in part and are being withheld in part. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the subject matter of withheld portions

steps.action: Withhold all; give volume, subject, Code cite

source.quote: The requested records are being entirely withheld. Such response shall identify with reasonable particularity the volume and subject matter of withheld records

steps.action: Report records not found; refer if known

source.quote: The requested records could not be found or do not exist. However, if the public body that received the request knows that another public body has the requested records, the response shall include contact information for the other public body.

steps.action: Charge no more than actual cost

source.quote: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost

gaps: Subsection A opens the records to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of in-state newspapers, magazines, radio and television stations; the text does not say how a request from anyone else is handled. The requester is typed as one private party.
The custodian may require the requester's name and legal address (§ 2.2-3704(A)); this optional exchange is not modelled as a step.

The text does not set a form or medium for the request (written, oral, electronic); it says only that the request must identify the records with reasonable specificity and need not mention the chapter to start the time limits (§ 2.2-3704(B)).

The written notice of possible charges is due 'Prior to conducting a search for records' (§ 2.2-3704(F)); the text does not say whether it is needed when no search is required. The model sends it before every response decision.

The response periods are tolled between notice of the cost estimate and the requester's response (§ 2.2-3704(F)) and between notice of the advance determination and the requester's response (§ 2.2-3704(H)); the five- and seven-work-day timers do not show the tolling.

The text does not say what the requester's response to a cost estimate may be (accept, narrow, abandon); the model shows only a response or the 30-day lapse to a deemed withdrawal. The estimating costs are applied toward the overall charges (§ 2.2-3704(F)).

A requester may both ask for a cost estimate and be required to pay a deposit; the model routes the estimate first and then the deposit. Processing waits for the deposit ('before continuing to process the request'), but the text gives no deadline or consequence if the deposit is never paid; the same is true of overdue prior charges under § 2.2-3704(I).

The 'additional seven work days' of § 2.2-3704(B)(4) are counted from the end of the first five-work-day period, and are available only if the not-practicable response was itself made within five working days; missing either period is modelled as the deemed denial of § 2.2-3704(E).

Subsection C does not tie the court petition to the not-practicable response or set a time for it; the model places it after that notice for requests of extraordinary volume or search length. The text does not say what the court may order, what happens to the response deadlines while the petition is pending, or how production proceeds under an agreement with the requester.

The grounds for withholding are in other sections of the chapter that are not included; the 'withheld_scope' input of the response tables stands in for them. Each withholding response must cite, for each category, the specific Code section authorising the withholding (§ 2.2-3704(B)(1)-(2)).

The text states no administrative appeal; a failure to respond is a deemed denial and a violation of the chapter (§ 2.2-3704(E)), but the enforcement remedy is elsewhere in the chapter and is not cited here. Whether a late response cures the deemed denial is not stated.
No new record need be created, but the public body may abstract or summarise information on agreed terms (§ 2.2-3704(D)); this is not modelled as a step.

Database records (§ 2.2-3704(G)) must be produced at actual cost in any tangible medium the requester identifies that the body uses in the regular course of business, with nonexempt records released even where exempt records are combined; these format rules are not modelled as steps.

When records were transferred for storage, maintenance or archiving, the transferring body, its successor or the possessor is the custodian for responding (§ 2.2-3704(J)); the model assumes the request reaches the right custodian.

The text does not say when charges are billed or paid relative to access; the model places the charge after records are supplied, in whole or in part. A local public body that charges may offer an electronic method of payment (§ 2.2-3704(F)); this option is not modelled.

The GIS charge may not exceed the public body's actual cost, except that topographical maps covering a contiguous area greater than 50 acres may be charged on a pro rata per acre basis (§ 2.2-3704(F)); the fee table summarises this in one rule.
